message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **long weekends** that Canadians could enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a public holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, giving you a 3‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1–3** | New Year’s Day (observed on Jan 2) | Jan 1 was a Sunday; the holiday was observed on Monday, Jan 2. |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Observed on Monday, Feb 20. |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday | Good Friday is a statutory holiday in most provinces. |
| **May 20–22** | Victoria Day | Observed on Monday, May 22. |
| **Jul 1–3** | Canada Day | Canada Day fell on Saturday, giving a 3‑day break. |
| **Sep 2–4** | Labour Day | Observed on Monday, Sep 4. |
| **Oct 7–9** | Thanksgiving | Observed on Monday, Oct 9. |
| **Nov 11–13** | Remembrance Day | Observed on Saturday, Nov 11. |
| **Dec 23–25** | Christmas Day | Christmas fell on Monday, Dec 25. |

> **Pro‑provincial notes**  
> • Some provinces (e.g., British Columbia, Nova Scotia, Newfoundland & Labrador) have additional holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in BC, Natal Day in NB, etc.).  
> • If you’re planning for a specific province, you’ll want to add those provincial holidays to the list above.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app. If you need the full list of provincial holidays or a more detailed calendar, let me know!
